findings.title: Boolean-based Blind SQL Injection in Login Form
findings.description: The username POST parameter in the PayBuddies login form is vulnerable to boolean-based blind SQL injection. The application differentiates between 'Invalid username' and 'Invalid password' responses, allowing an attacker to extract database information character by character. Database: payroll_db, Table: users (user_id, username, password). Admin credentials: admin / MD5 hash 7d39307ae824e70052c0aa16816a9b16. Time-based SQLi also confirmed working.
findings.evidence: sqlmap confirmed: Parameter: username (POST), Type: boolean-based blind, Title: AND boolean-based blind - WHERE or HAVING clause, Payload: username=admin' AND 2054=2054-- TAVw&password=test1234&submit=submit. Backend DBMS: MySQL 8.0.42 on Ubuntu.

findings.title: Reflected XSS via name parameter
findings.description: The 'name' GET parameter on /page is reflected in an tag without proper sanitization. Characters <, (, ), and ` are filtered, but HTML entity encoding of parentheses (( and )) bypasses the filter and executes JavaScript.
